To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we provide a theoretical framework for measuring the robustness of explainers, and (2) we empirically show the connection between the robustness of a predictor and the robustness of the explanations for it.
We formalize the notion of explainer astutenes, which is analogous to the astuteness notion in classifiers.

1. We define a novel notion of explainer astuteneness that quantifies how similar an explainer's explanations are for similar data inputs and show that this is related to the Lipschitz property of the prediction model
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability of explainers and how it is related to the reliability of the prediction model itself.
the reliability of explainer methods.
the question of whether a classifier’s Lipschitzness affects the reliability of its explanations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the astuteness guarantees we have provided in the theoretical section of our paper are indeed empirically validated.
the astuteness (and thus reliability) of explainers can be improved by making the classifier more Lipschitz.
the Lipschitz constant of the prediction function is a good predictor of the astuteness, i.e. the stability of the explanations of an explainer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the astuteness and robustness of an explainer is highly dependent on the Lipschitz property of the classifier, and that a locally smooth classifier lends itself to a locally robust explainer.
we show that for a variety of explainer methods, if the prediction function is locally smooth, then the explanations are locally robust.
for locally smooth prediction functions, the astuteness is a function of the Lipschitz constants of the explainer, which is a function of its hyperparameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the astuteness and the Lipschitz properties of the prediction function and the explainer are intimately related.
the Lipschitz constant of the underlying classifier is a crucial determinant in how robust the explanation is.
the astuteness (robustness) of explainers can be improved by using more Lipschitz classifiers.
